gaps.wanted: The QFX3600 datasheet. Searched juniper.net for it and found only the hardware guide; the product is end of life. The weight, dimensions and power are the guide's.
A photograph of either side. The image-library address pattern returns 404 for this model, so every measure is read from the guide's flat vector drawings and the colour is estimated.

Table 5 gives the width as 16.9 in (42.9 cm) and the guide's flat figures 3 and 4 have the aspect of a 17.4 in body (9.98 against 9.71). The table is carried for the chassis and the drawings are scaled to it, which squeezes the positions by up to 3 percent across; a photograph or a datasheet row would settle it.

Table 25 prints 341 W as the DC typical power consumption and 252 W as the maximum. A typical figure above the maximum is impossible, so they are carried the other way round (252 typical, 341 maximum) as an estimate. The AC figures (Table 23) are 255 W typical and 345 W maximum.
The dates of the end of sale and end of service. Juniper's technical bulletin TSB17796 lists the end-of-service dates of the product's parts; the bulletin could not be fetched.

The part numbers of the four pairs of brackets (two-post front or rear, two-post mid-mount, four-post fixed rail and four-post adjustable rail) and their depth ranges. The guide describes them in prose and in figures 22 to 24 and gives the rack depth (19.3 to 36 in) and no part number.
The front panel of the QFX3600-I Interconnect (QFX3600-I-16Q-AFI and -AFO, guide Table 11), which the guide refers to a topic of another document. The rear panel is shared (figure 4). Not modelled.
The two grounding points for M5 screws 15.86 mm apart (guide page 60). Figure 4 draws one small block and no hole spacing, so the block is drawn as it is.
The sliding panel at the top right of the front that carries the serial number label and serves as the ESD point (figure 3, callout 4). It is drawn as a plate; the guide gives no more of it.
The size of the LCD in characters. The guide says it shows the host name and the number of active alarms and gives no character count, so it is drawn as a window.
The Junos mark beside the chassis lamps, which is a logo and is not drawn.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation. It is drawn with the kit's neutral usb2 skin.
A flat drawing or photograph of the lid, the underside and the side panels.

chassis.note: guide Table 5 (shared with the QFX3600-I): 1.74 in (4.4 cm) high; 16.9 in (42.9 cm) wide excluding the mounting brackets, 19.2 in (48.8 cm) including them; 19.3 in (49 cm) deep excluding the FRU handles and locking levers, 19.4 in (49.3 cm) including them; 20.5 lb (9.3 kg) with FRUs, 14.6 lb (6.6 kg) without. The body is drawn: the brackets are not part of it. The rack requirements (Table 21) put four-post rails 19.3 to 36 in apart.

chassis-lamps.note: Figure 6 and Table 9: three lamps in a column to the right of the LCD, Power, Status (legended OK/!) and Fan, 4.9 mm apart. Power is green when the switch is on and blinks amber on a temperature or voltage shutdown; Status is green when Junos OS is loaded, blinks intermittently for the beacon and blinks amber on a software error; Fan is green when the fan trays are normal and blinks amber on a fan tray error. Their icons are drawn beside them. The Junos mark in the drawing is a logo and is not drawn.

colour.note: No photograph is held and the drawings are line art, so the colour is a neutral steel grey, not a reading of the metal.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide supplies four pairs of brackets with the switch: front or rear two-post, mid-mount two-post, fixed-rail four-post and adjustable-rail four-post (Table 21 and the mounting topics). No part number is given for any of them, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The body is the 16.9 in chassis, without the 19.2 in brackets.

front-and-rear.note: The guide calls the port side the front panel and the FRU side the rear panel, and the library does the same (the QFX3500 guide names its two sides the other way round). The guide's AFI (airflow in, FRU-to-port) is the library's back-to-front and AFO (port-to-FRU) its front-to-back.

fru-side-layout.note: Figure 4 (flat) with Tables 11 and 12. Supply 0 at the left end, a two-hole grounding point, fan trays 0 to 2 on a 86.3 mm pitch and supply 1 at the right end. The supplies are 54.8 x 39.8 mm (the size of the same JPSU-650W unit in the QFX5100, which the drawing agrees with to 3 percent, 56 mm across the frame) and the fan trays 80.0 x 41.6 mm. The grounding point is drawn as one small block 8.0 x 6.7 mm; the guide says the chassis has grounding points for M5 screws 0.625 in (15.86 mm) apart (page 60), which does not fit the block, so the block is drawn as it is and the spacing is a gap.

gate-1.note: The guide's figures 3 and 4 (pages 26 and 27, drawings g050202 and g050203) are flat vector drawings of the two sides. Their body outline measures 304.13 x 30.48 pt, an aspect of 9.98 against the table's 16.9 / 1.74 = 9.71, 2.8 percent out (9.98 is the aspect of a 17.4 in body, the QFX3500's width). The two figures of one guide disagree, so each axis is scaled to its own table figure, 1.4106 mm/pt across and 1.450 down, and every position is good to about 1.5 mm. The vector coordinates were read from the PDF page itself, not from a render.

lifecycle.note: Juniper's support page for the QFX3500 labels it end of life and the technical bulletin that extends the end of service of its parts (TSB17796) lists a QFX3600 part (QFX3600-16Q-AFIS) among them; the bulletin could not be fetched from this worker, so no date is stated, and the QFX3600 support page was not read. Estimated, because it is read from a search result and the bulletin was not opened.

models.note: guide Table 11: QFX3600-16Q-AFI (FRU-to-port), QFX3600-16Q-AFO (port-to-FRU), and the Interconnect models QFX3600-I-16Q-AFI and QFX3600-I-16Q-AFO. The two QFX3600-16Q models are the orderable configurations. The QFX3600-I shares the chassis table and the rear panel (figure 4 is captioned for both) but its front panel is described in a topic of another document ("Front Panel of a QFX3600-I Interconnect Device") that this slice does not hold, so the Interconnect is not modelled and is left for a later change. A QFX3600 can be configured as a Node device or as an Interconnect device in a QFX3000-M system (guide, Overview); that is software, not a configuration here. Neither the guide nor anything held names a DC chassis model: the DC supplies are listed as units (Tables 14, 15) and the DC power figures are given for the chassis (Table 25), so the two DC builds are illustrations (`example`) that do not export a device type.

modules.note: The two power supplies and the three fan trays are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component (Table 6). The supplies are the 650 W JPSU-650W units, reused from the QFX5100 by part number (juniper/qfx5100-jpsu-650w-ac-afo, -ac-afi, -dc-afo and -dc-afi: the guide gives the one unit to the QFX3500, QFX3600 and QFX3600-I, Tables 14 and 15). The fan trays are QFXC01-FANBO and QFXC01-FANBI (Table 12). The guide says to fit a blank panel in an empty supply slot and gives it no part number, so no blank is modelled and no empty-bay configuration is offered. The supplies carry their own fans. The management ports, the LCD and the lamps are part of the chassis here, not a board: the QFX3600 guide lists no management board among its FRUs (Table 6).

port-lamps.note: Figure 5 and Tables 7 and 8: two lamps on every port, legended LA (Link/Activity) above ST (Status), a stack of two to the left of each cage, 3.7 mm apart in the drawing's lamp circles (3.55 pt). Link/Activity is green when a link is established and blinks with activity (a QSFP+ access port stays lit while any of its four 10 GbE breakout links is up); Status is green when a transceiver is installed. The lamp positions are read off figure 3 by lamp circle.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off figure 3: Q0 to Q15, Q0 and Q1 over each other in the first column, Q2 and Q3 in the second, and so on, the even number above the upper cage and the odd number below the lower one. The ports are numbered as printed. Interface names (the guide's xle and xe names of its Port Type topics) are not printed on the unit and are not written to the manifest.

ports.note: Figure 3. Eight columns of QSFP+ cages in two rows: cage faces 19.95 mm wide (the registry's 18.5 x 9.58 aperture is centred on them) on a column pitch of 33.47 mm, the first at 90.37 mm, wide because the two lamps of a port sit between the columns. The registry's 19.0 QSFP+ ganged pitch is a floor, not the figure, so the drawing's pitch is used.

power.note: guide Table 23 (AC): typical 255 W, maximum 345 W; 100 to 240 VAC, 4 A at 100 VAC or 2 A at 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz. Table 25 (DC): -40 to -72 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 8 A maximum; the table prints 341 W as the typical and 252 W as the maximum consumption, which cannot both be right (a typical above the maximum), so the DC figures are a gap and are carried the other way round, 252 W typical and 341 W maximum, as an estimate.

row-pitch.note: Figure 3: the cage faces centre 19.07 and 32.93 mm below the top edge, a row pitch of 13.86 mm.

stack-orientation.note: The flat figure draws the cages with no latch tongue that could be read. The lower row is turned 180, the library's stack convention for a two-row QSFP+ block, which is an assumption.

vents.note: Figure 3 draws hexagonal holes above and below the port block and around the console and USB jacks. They are drawn as vent strips; the hexagon pitch (4.4 mm along the strip) is estimated as the drawing's hexagons are too small to measure to a tenth.
